captions.instagram:
How do electric scooters work?

An electric scooter has no engine, no gears and no clutch: just 160 finger-sized cells, a motor hidden inside the back wheel, and a box of switches that flips its coils hundreds of times a second. Take one apart in 3D and see why it costs a few paise per kilometre.

→ An electric scooter has no engine, no fuel tank and no gearbox: just a battery, a motor and a controller.
→ Cells in parallel add capacity; groups in series add voltage. Sixteen groups of ten make 57.6 volts and 2.88 kWh.
→ Magnets ride on the wheel; coils sit on the axle. The controller lights the three phases in turn to pull the wheel round.
→ Current gives torque, even at standstill. Voltage sets the top speed, where back-EMF catches up.
→ Tyres, air and hills take the energy. Air drag grows with speed squared, so riding fast eats range.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/escooterclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do electric scooters work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
An electric scooter has no engine, no gears and no clutch: just 160 finger-sized cells, a motor hidden inside the back wheel, and a box of switches that flips its coils hundreds of times a second. Take one apart in 3D and see why it costs a few paise per kilometre.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/escooterclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/escooterclear

In this video:
• Three parts do the work. A battery pack under the floor, a motor built into the rear wheel, and a controller that links them.
• Cells in series and parallel. One lithium-ion cell gives about 3.6 V.
• Magnets on the wheel, coils on the axle. The hub motor's drum carries magnets; the fixed stator carries three sets of coils.
• Where the energy goes. At 40 km/h the scooter needs about 19 Wh per km at the wheel: rolling resistance and, more and more with speed, air drag.
• Braking back, charging in. Slowing down, the motor works as a generator, but from 40 km/h the motion holds only about 3 Wh, so the friction brakes still do the real stopping.
• Safety first. After scooter fires in 2022, India added tougher battery tests to the AIS-156 standard: smarter BMS, cell spacing, extra fuses, temperature sensors and an overheat warning.
